title: A Three-body Problem and LISA
summary: From a co-rotating three-body system to the relative motion of a triangular space-based gravitational-wave detector.
attribution: 42nd International Physics Olympiad, Bangkok, Thailand, theoretical competition, 12 July 2011. Figure 2 credits D. A. Shaddock, An Overview of the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna, Publications of the Astronomical Society of Australia 26 (2009), 128–132.

context.value: Two gravitating masses M and m move in circular orbits of radii R and r about their common centre of mass O. A third body of infinitesimal mass μ may move in a circular orbit in the same plane, remaining stationary relative to the other two masses. The geometry is Figure 1 on original page 1.

For 1.4, use the LISA design described in the 2011 paper, not a present-day mission specification. Three identical spacecraft lie at the corners of an equilateral triangle with arms about 5.0 million kilometres long. The constellation follows an Earth-like orbit around the Sun, trailing Earth by 20 degrees. Each spacecraft follows a slightly inclined individual orbit; the triangle appears to roll around its centre once per year. Laser interferometry detects tiny changes in arm lengths. Figures 2 and 3 are on original pages 2 and 3.

parts.title: Angular velocity of two gravitating bodies
parts.prompt: Determine the angular velocity of the line joining M and m in terms of R, r, M, m, and G.
parts.model: $$\omega_0=\text{angular velocity of the line joining the two masses}$$

parts.title: A stationary third body
parts.prompt: Place an infinitesimal mass μ in a coplanar circular orbit about O, stationary relative to M and m and not collinear with them, as in Figure 1. In terms of R and r, determine each of the following distances.
items: 1.2.3: from μ to the centre of mass O.

parts.title: Radial oscillations for equal masses
parts.prompt: Now take M = m. Give μ a small radial perturbation along Oμ. Assuming its angular momentum is conserved, find the angular frequency of its oscillation about the unperturbed position, in terms of the unperturbed orbital angular velocity.

parts.title: Relative speed in the LISA constellation
parts.prompt: Using the LISA configuration in the shared setup and original Figures 2–3, determine the relative speed of one spacecraft with respect to another in the plane containing the three spacecraft.
